question.:question/problem:
![](/tmp/ca9837-templates-5ek4tgt5/17592186179742/d8544577858d06746ca1-prompt.png)

The gray arrows show the non-constant field $\mathbf F(x,y)=\left(4 y,- 9 x\right)$. The blue path lies on $\frac{x^2}{4}+\frac{y^2}{9}=1$. Let $C$ be three-quarters of this ellipse, traversed counterclockwise from $A=(0,-3)$ to $B=(-2,0)$. Let $-C$ denote the same path with the orientation reversed.

Which statements are true? **Select all that apply.**
question.:question/worked-solution:
The line integral measures signed work: assistance contributes positive work, opposition negative work, and perpendicular force zero work.

The field is tangent to the ellipse. Along the indicated orientation, the field points against the motion at every point. Every contribution is therefore negative.

![](/tmp/ca9837-templates-5ek4tgt5/17592186179742/d8544577858d06746ca1-forward.png)

Thus $\int_{C}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r<0$. Reversing the path reverses every displacement while keeping the field fixed:

$$
\int_{-C}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r=-\int_C\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r
$$

![](/tmp/ca9837-templates-5ek4tgt5/17592186179742/d8544577858d06746ca1-reverse.png)

Therefore $\int_{-C}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r>0$.

Statement 1, $\int_{-C}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r<0$, is **false**.

Statement 2, $\int_{C}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r=0$, is **false**.

Statement 3, $\int_{C}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r<0$, is **true**.

knowledge_point.title: Interpreting the Sign of a Line Integral Over a Non-Constant Vector Field

question.:question/problem:
![](/tmp/ca9837-templates-5ek4tgt5/17592186179742/c77b9985c70f9254a356-prompt.png)

The gray arrows show the non-constant field $\mathbf F(x,y)=\left(x - y + 3,0\right)$. The blue path lies on $\frac{x^2}{9}+\frac{y^2}{4}=1$. Let $C$ be the half of this ellipse in $x>0$ from $A=(0,-2)$ to $B=(0,2)$. Let $-C$ denote the same path with the orientation reversed.

Which statements are true? **Select all that apply.**
question.:question/worked-solution:
The line integral measures signed work: assistance contributes positive work, opposition negative work, and perpendicular force zero work.

The field points rightward everywhere on this arc. On the first half it does positive work; on the second half it does negative work. The work parallel to the other coordinate axis is zero.

Pair the point on the first half with its reflection on the second half at the same $x=v$, where $v>0$. Their $y$ coordinates are $- u$ and $u$, where $u>0$. Their small $x$ displacements have equal magnitudes and opposite signs. The signed field components at the paired points differ by

$$
\begin{aligned}F_{x,1}-F_{x,2}&=\left(u + v + 3\right)-\left(- u + v + 3\right) \\ &=2 u\end{aligned}
$$

The first displacement in $x$ is positive. Multiplying it by the displayed force difference gives positive work for every pair. The positive contribution dominates, so the total work has that sign. Equal endpoint coordinates alone would not establish cancellation.

![](/tmp/ca9837-templates-5ek4tgt5/17592186179742/c77b9985c70f9254a356-forward.png)

Thus $\int_{C}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r>0$. Reversing the path reverses every displacement while keeping the field fixed:

$$
\int_{-C}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r=-\int_C\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r
$$

![](/tmp/ca9837-templates-5ek4tgt5/17592186179742/c77b9985c70f9254a356-reverse.png)

Therefore $\int_{-C}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r<0$.

Statement 1, $\int_{C}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r=0$, is **false**.

Statement 2, $\int_{C}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r<0$, is **false**.

Statement 3, $\int_{-C}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r<0$, is **true**.

knowledge_point.title: Interpreting the Sign of a Line Integral Over a Non-Constant Vector Field

question.:question/problem:
![](/tmp/ca9837-templates-5ek4tgt5/17592186179742/0ac127bb1b620f839501-prompt.png)

The gray arrows show the non-constant field $\mathbf F(x,y)=\left(9 x - 4 y,9 x + 4 y\right)$. The blue path lies on $\frac{x^2}{4}+\frac{y^2}{9}=1$. Let $C$ be one-half of this ellipse, traversed counterclockwise from $A=(0,-3)$ to $B=(0,3)$. Let $-C$ denote the same path with the orientation reversed.

Which statements are true? **Select all that apply.**
question.:question/worked-solution:
The line integral measures signed work: assistance contributes positive work, opposition negative work, and perpendicular force zero work.

Separate the field into its normal and tangent components:

$$
\mathbf F=\left(9 x,4 y\right)+\left(- 4 y,9 x\right)
$$

The first component is proportional to the gradient of the displayed ellipse equation. It is perpendicular to the curve and contributes *zero work*. The second component is tangent and points with the indicated motion throughout the arc. Thus the total work is positive.

![](/tmp/ca9837-templates-5ek4tgt5/17592186179742/0ac127bb1b620f839501-forward.png)

Thus $\int_{C}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r>0$. Reversing the path reverses every displacement while keeping the field fixed:

$$
\int_{-C}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r=-\int_C\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r
$$

![](/tmp/ca9837-templates-5ek4tgt5/17592186179742/0ac127bb1b620f839501-reverse.png)

Therefore $\int_{-C}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r<0$.

Statement 1, $\int_{C}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r=0$, is **false**.

Statement 2, $\int_{C}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r<0$, is **false**.

Statement 3, $\int_{-C}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r<0$, is **true**.
